name: Zechariah

overview.author: Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, a priest and prophet among the returned exiles (1:1; Nehemiah 12:16).
overview.date: Chapters 1–8 date from 520–518 BC; chapters 9–14 are undated and may come from later in Zechariah’s life.
overview.audience: The returned exiles in Jerusalem, rebuilding the temple alongside Haggai’s ministry.
overview.setting: A small, struggling community under Persian rule, led by Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest.
overview.purpose: To call the people to return to God, encourage temple rebuilding through visions of God’s care, and reveal the coming Messiah, King and Shepherd, and God’s final victory.
overview.structure: A call to return (1:1–6), eight night visions (1:7–6:8), the crowning of Joshua (6:9–15), questions about fasting (7–8), and two oracles about the coming King and the final day (9–14).

themes.title: Return to God
themes.text: “Return to me... and I will return to you” (1:3).

themes.title: God’s Jealous Love for Zion
themes.text: God is zealous for Jerusalem and will dwell in her midst.

themes.title: The Spirit’s Power
themes.text: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit” (4:6).

themes.title: The Branch, Priest and King
themes.text: A coming one will build the temple and unite priest and king.

themes.title: True Religion
themes.text: God desires justice, kindness, and mercy rather than empty fasts.

themes.title: The Messiah King and Shepherd
themes.text: Humble King, pierced one, struck Shepherd.

themes.title: God’s Final Reign
themes.text: “The LORD will be king over all the earth” (14:9).

keyVerses.quote: Return to me, says the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
Behold, your king is coming to you; righteous and having salvation is he, humble and mounted on a donkey.
When they look on me, on him whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him.
And the LORD will be king over all the earth.

christInBook.text: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey (Matthew 21:4–5; John 12:14–15).
Thirty pieces of silver thrown to the potter (Matthew 27:9–10).
They will look on Him whom they pierced (John 19:37; Revelation 1:7).
“Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered” (Matthew 26:31).
The Branch who is both priest and king (Hebrews 7; 8:1).
The Branch removes iniquity in a single day.

crossReferences.note: God’s final dwelling with His people.

reflection: How does “Return to me... and I will return to you” (1:3) invite you today?
Where are you relying on might or power instead of God’s Spirit (4:6)?
Zechariah 4:10 warns against despising the day of small things. What small beginnings has God given you?
How does Jesus’ humble entry on a donkey shape your idea of kingship?
Zechariah 7:9–10 calls for justice and mercy. Who around you needs that?

chapterList.title: Return to Me
chapterList.summary: God calls the people: “Return to me... and I will return to you.” Do not be like your fathers. In the first vision, a man on a red horse among myrtle trees reports the earth at rest, while Jerusalem lies in ruins. God declares, “I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem,” and will rebuild His house. A second vision of four horns and four craftsmen shows God will break the nations that scattered Judah.
questions: What does God promise when people return (1:3)?
How does the angel intercede for Jerusalem (1:12)?
What do the horns and craftsmen represent?

chapterList.title: The Measuring Line
chapterList.summary: A man goes to measure Jerusalem, but God says it will be a city without walls because of its many people, and “I will be to her a wall of fire all around.” God will dwell in the midst of Zion, and many nations will join themselves to Him. “Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD.”
questions: Why would Jerusalem need no walls (2:4–5)?
What does it mean that God’s people are “the apple of his eye” (2:8)?
How does 2:11 point to Gentiles joining God’s people?

chapterList.title: Joshua the High Priest
chapterList.summary: Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of the LORD in filthy garments, with Satan accusing him. The LORD rebukes Satan, takes away the filthy clothes, and clothes Joshua with pure vestments: “I have taken your iniquity away from you.” God promises His servant the Branch and will remove iniquity in a single day.
questions: What do the filthy garments represent?
How does God answer Satan’s accusation (3:2)?
How does this picture salvation in Christ (Romans 8:33–34; Isaiah 61:10)?

chapterList.title: The Lampstand and Olive Trees
chapterList.summary: Zechariah sees a golden lampstand fed by two olive trees. The message to Zerubbabel: “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.” The mountain before him will become a plain, and he will finish the temple. “Whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice.”
questions: What does the oil supply represent (4:6)?
What “mountain” might God level for you (4:7)?
Why should we not despise small beginnings (4:10)?

chapterList.title: The Flying Scroll and the Basket
chapterList.summary: A huge flying scroll carries a curse against thieves and those who swear falsely. A woman in a basket, representing wickedness, is carried away to Babylon.
questions: What sins does the flying scroll target?
What does removing wickedness to Babylon picture?
How does God deal with sin among His people?

chapterList.title: The Chariots and the Crown
chapterList.summary: Four chariots go out to patrol the earth. Zechariah is told to crown Joshua the high priest: “Behold, the man whose name is the Branch... he shall build the temple of the LORD... and shall sit and rule on his throne. And there shall be a priest on his throne.”
questions: Why is it striking that a priest is crowned?
Who is the Branch who unites priest and king?
How does Hebrews describe Jesus as priest-king (Hebrews 8:1)?

chapterList.title: Fasting Without Heart
chapterList.summary: Bethel’s people ask whether they should keep fasting over Jerusalem’s destruction. God asks whether their fasts were really for Him. He calls them to “render true judgments, show kindness and mercy... do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the sojourner, or the poor.” Their fathers refused and were scattered.
questions: What question does God ask about their fasting (7:5–6)?
What does God really want (7:9–10)?
Why did their fathers’ hearts become like diamond (7:12)?

chapterList.title: Jerusalem Restored
chapterList.summary: God is jealous for Zion and will return to dwell in Jerusalem. Old people will sit in the streets and children will play. Fasts will become feasts. Many peoples will come to seek the LORD, and ten men will grab a Jew’s robe saying, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.”
questions: What picture of peace does 8:4–5 give?
What does God command His people (8:16–17)?
How does 8:23 picture the nations coming to God?

chapterList.title: Your King Is Coming
chapterList.summary: God will judge Israel’s neighbors. “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion!... Behold, your king is coming to you; righteous and having salvation is he, humble and mounted on a donkey.” He will speak peace to the nations. Because of the blood of the covenant, God will set prisoners free.
questions: How was 9:9 fulfilled (Matthew 21:1–9)?
What kind of King comes on a donkey?
What does “blood of my covenant” (9:11) point to?

chapterList.title: The LORD Cares for His Flock
chapterList.summary: Ask the LORD for rain, not idols. The people wander like sheep without a shepherd. God will care for His flock, make Judah strong, and bring back the scattered. “I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they shall walk in his name.”
questions: Why did the people wander (10:2)?
What does God promise to do for His flock (10:6–12)?
How does Jesus see crowds “like sheep without a shepherd” (Matthew 9:36)?

chapterList.title: The Rejected Shepherd
chapterList.summary: Zechariah acts as a shepherd of a flock doomed to slaughter. He breaks two staffs, Favor and Union. He is paid thirty pieces of silver, a lordly price, which he throws to the potter in the house of the LORD. A worthless shepherd will come.
questions: What does the thirty pieces of silver signify?
How is this fulfilled with Judas (Matthew 27:3–10)?
How do worthless shepherds harm the flock (11:16–17)?

chapterList.title: Him Whom They Have Pierced
chapterList.summary: God will make Jerusalem a cup of staggering and a heavy stone to the nations. He will pour out a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy, “so that, when they look on me, on him whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child.”
questions: Who is the pierced one (John 19:37)?
What does a “spirit of grace and pleas for mercy” produce?
How does grief over sin lead to salvation?

chapterList.title: A Fountain for Cleansing
chapterList.summary: A fountain will be opened to cleanse from sin and uncleanness. Idols and false prophets will be removed. “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.” A third will be refined like silver and gold: “They will call upon my name, and I will answer them.”
questions: What does the fountain represent (13:1)?
How does Jesus apply 13:7 (Matthew 26:31)?
How does God refine His people (13:9)?

chapterList.title: The LORD Will Be King
chapterList.summary: The nations gather against Jerusalem, but the LORD goes out to fight. His feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits. Living waters flow from Jerusalem. “The LORD will be king over all the earth.” Survivors of the nations worship, and even cooking pots are inscribed “Holy to the LORD.”
questions: What does 14:4 picture about the LORD’s coming?
What do living waters symbolize (14:8)?
What does it mean that ordinary things will be “Holy to the LORD” (14:20–21)?

tagline: Return to me: visions of hope and the coming humble King
readingPlan: 14 chapters: one chapter a day takes 14 days; two a day takes about 7 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
